title: Plan cryptographic agility and evaluate quantum claims: concept decisions 2
teachingQuestion: Which cryptographic dependency should move first, and what controlled transition proves it remains protected?
focalInsight: Algorithm names are only one part of an accountable inventory, compatibility, rollout, rollback, and retirement decision.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: Ml Kem
nodes.definition: NIST FIPS 203 standardized ML-KEM for post-quantum key establishment.
nodes.detail: NIST FIPS 203 standardized ML-KEM for post-quantum key establishment.
nodes.decision: Use only for its key-establishment role within an approved, tested protocol profile.
nodes.failureExample: A supplier claims ML-KEM signs releases or secures every protocol layer.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: ML-KEM establishes a shared secret; it is not a signature algorithm.

nodes.label: Ml Dsa
nodes.definition: NIST FIPS 204 standardized ML-DSA as a post-quantum digital-signature algorithm.
nodes.detail: NIST FIPS 204 standardized ML-DSA as a post-quantum digital-signature algorithm.
nodes.decision: Use when the required role is signing with compatible implementation, certificate, and verifier support.
nodes.failureExample: A migration replaces a key-establishment mechanism with ML-DSA without redesigning the protocol role.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: ML-DSA is for signatures, not shared-secret establishment.

nodes.label: Slh Dsa
nodes.definition: NIST FIPS 205 standardized SLH-DSA as a post-quantum digital-signature algorithm.
nodes.detail: NIST FIPS 205 standardized SLH-DSA as a post-quantum digital-signature algorithm.
nodes.decision: Select only through approved profiles and testing of its signature, performance, and interoperability role.
nodes.failureExample: A team assumes ML-DSA and SLH-DSA are interchangeable without a policy or compatibility decision.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Both are signature standards; profile selection and deployment evidence still matter.

nodes.label: Crypto Inventory Owner
nodes.definition: Accountable role that maintains the mapping from cryptographic use to system, dependency, data, and lifecycle.
nodes.detail: Accountable role that maintains the mapping from cryptographic use to system, dependency, data, and lifecycle.
nodes.decision: Assign when an inventory entry must remain current through change and deprecation.
nodes.failureExample: A migration list names algorithms but nobody owns embedded library discovery.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: An inventory is useful only if a named owner maintains it.

nodes.label: Migration Change Authority
nodes.definition: Role authorized to approve profiles, exceptions, rollout, rollback, and retirement in a cryptographic transition.
nodes.detail: Role authorized to approve profiles, exceptions, rollout, rollback, and retirement in a cryptographic transition.
nodes.decision: Assign before pilot and production changes so fallback cannot silently reinstate deprecated protection.
nodes.failureExample: An emergency rollback restores a weak protocol with no expiry or approval.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Migration authority governs both adoption and safe rollback.
